desc: Ideation: identify problem as thresholded Levenshtein with K<=20 and banded DP around main diagonal.
Implement a complete first-pass solution: bytes input parsing, length-difference rejection, and furthest-reaching diagonal (Landau-Vishkin/Myers) DP with C-speed bytes LCP snake extension.
Optimize Python performance: only ~(K+1)(2K+1) ≈ 861 Python-level states total; all heavy comparison work delegated to C-speed bytes slicing/memcmp — no banded cell-by-cell loop needed.

Verify correctness: orchestrator re-reviewed the recurrence (substitution/deletion/insertion moves with out-of-grid rejection, frontier propagation along i=n and j=m, snake extension, per-d termination check covering "at most K"), index bounds (off=K+1, size=2K+3 covers k∈[-K-1,K+1]), NEG sentinel handling, and edge cases (equal strings, single substitution, insert/delete-only, length-diff rejection, d=0 target check). Worker hand-verified all three samples plus edge cases.
Finalize stdout behavior: prints exactly "Yes\n" or "No\n" with early exit on first reachable d ≤ K.
